summary: Restore schneiden in the decapitation example
rationale: The example means cutting off a head; 56/96 explicitly has “schneidet ... den Kopf ab”. Scheidet is a different verb.
The supplied translation of 72/6 says “jeder Wespe”; the immediately preceding 72/5 also identifies each emerging insect as a Wespe. The English rendering changes the insect to a bee.

summary: Algae example differs from the cited verb and may belong to qyš
rationale: The opening clause is in 75/91, and 75/92 continues “I kavzayo, qəša”, translated “Schöpfe die Algen ab”. The existing qyš imperative quotes the same phrase and citation as “i=kavz-ayo, quš-a”. The present qyṣ example instead has ṣ and translates “Cut”. It is unclear whether the editor intended an independent qyṣ wording or miscopied the qyš example. Do not adopt the automatic alternative 75/111, which narrates fetching the algae and is not this utterance.

summary: Remove the extra syllable in the word for their wings
rationale: The corresponding phrase in 95/99 is “koqoyəṣ ač=čangaṯṯe, kodoralle”. The entry inserts an extra ta into the noun, beyond clitic or accent normalization.
The barber cut his hair: the supplied translation of 28/42 reads “der schnitt ihm die Haare”.
